meta.title: Arduino Uno → HC-SR04 ultrasonic ranger
meta.intro: A minimal distance-sensor build that shows off the module registry: the sensor is declared as just "module": "hc-sr04" — no hand-listed pins — and the validator still knows VCC is power, GND is ground, and TRIG/ECHO are signals, so it rejects (for example) wiring 5V onto TRIG.
notes: The HC-SR04 is a 5V part — power VCC from the Uno's 5V pin, not 3V3.

notes.html: HC-SR04 ECHO is 5V logic. It is safe straight into a 5V Uno, but on a 3.3V MCU (ESP32/Pi) divide or level-shift ECHO first.

notes: Pins came from the built-in hc-sr04 module: VCC (power), TRIG (signal in), ECHO (signal out), GND. Author pins/roles override the defaults when needed.
buildOrder: Power: Uno 5V → HC-SR04 VCC, and a common GND.
In code, pulse TRIG HIGH for 10µs, then time the ECHO HIGH pulse; distance_cm = pulse_us / 58.
checks: TRIG and ECHO on two distinct digital pins (D2/D3 here) — not swapped with power/ground.
